note: VERIFICATION ONLY, covers=0. The UI colour/render check the Gamma->Linear switch of 2026-10-30 needed (docs/open_items.json row ui-colour-check). Drives the REAL shell on the REAL Game.unity (Login -> Character -> world, HeroScreenProbe's reflection pattern) and renders the LIVE panel at 1920x1080 to scratchpad/shots/ui_login.png, ui_character.png and ui_hud.png (the last composited over the scene camera's own frame). HOW THE PANEL IS CAPTURED, since this was the hard part: a screen-space-overlay panel is NOT drawn by Camera.Render() into a RenderTexture - URP gates overlay UI on UniversalCameraData.rendersOverlayUI = rendersUIOverlay && resolveToScreen, and resolveToScreen is `targetTexture == null` (UniversalCameraData.cs:307,384), so pointing the camera at a target texture silently drops the whole UI with every 'UI installed' flag still true. What works is PanelSettings.targetTexture (makes it an OFFSCREEN panel) plus a hand-driven repaint, because edit mode has no player loop: UnityEngine.UIElements.UIElementsRuntimeUtility's internal UpdatePanels() + RepaintPanels() + RenderOffscreenPanels() by reflection. That is the path that produced pixels (UIRENDER path=runtimeUtility, 2,073,600 non-transparent px on the full-screen shell); the fallback path (the panel object's own Update()/Repaint(Event)) was never needed. The target is ARGB32 + RenderTextureReadWrite.sRGB so GetPixels32 hands back the final display bytes, directly comparable with the hex. The panel MUST be pinned to that target before anything is measured: with no target texture a panel lays out at Screen.width x Screen.height, which is 640x480 in batch mode, and every worldBound would be in a different space from the pixels.

FIX, no new JS coverage claimed. New UiBootstrap.FillPanel(root), applied in ShellView, CharacterView, SettingsView, CreditsView and CinemaLetterboxView right after uxml.CloneTree(this). THE WRAPPER-COLLAPSE TRAP: in src/index.html the full-screen layers (#screen-login, .hangar, #settings, #credits, the cinema letterbox) are children of <body> and their `inset: 0` resolves against the viewport. In this port each is cloned INTO a C# VisualElement subclass - an extra level the DOM never had - and that wrapper is a flex child with height:auto whose only child is absolutely positioned, i.e. out of flow, so the wrapper computes to 1920x0 and every inset:0 layer inside inherits zero height. Nothing throws and the screen is not empty: text and content-sized boxes still draw (overflow is visible by default), so it LOOKS present while every full-bleed background and every vertical centring is gone. Measured: the login screen covered 2.2% of a 1920x1080 frame (45,729 of 2,073,600 px) with no backdrop; after the fix, 100%. UiShotProbe carries a CONTROL ARM that clones the same Shell.uxml into an unstyled wrapper on the same panel and prints its rect (1920x0, UISHOTRECT arm=control_noFillPanel), so the claim that FillPanel is what fixes it is measured and not asserted. PickingMode.Ignore is part of the fix: a full-screen wrapper with default picking would swallow every pointer event in the panel, including while its own content is display:none (SettingsView/CreditsView are built once and hidden), which would have broken the target card and the skill bar.

FIX, no new JS coverage claimed. USS HAS NO `em` UNIT, and the importer does not reject just the declaration - it fails the WHOLE file and leaves an EMPTY StyleSheet that still loads, is still named, and is still attached to the view. Character.uss had 17 `letter-spacing: 0.0Nem` transcribed literally from src/style.css and imported with ZERO rules; the personage screen rendered with every element present and nothing styled - full-width stacked rows, default grey Unity buttons, no columns, no panels, no padding - with no error in any log. Proven by UiShotProbe: UISTYLE arm=character sheets=1 [Character] while .hangar's own `padding: 74px 44px 44px` resolved to paddingTop=0, and by the first ui_character.png. Converted to the px each em meant (CSS em == the element's own font-size, e.g. 0.06em at font-size:15px = 0.9px); after the fix the sheet has 75 rules and .hangar resolves 74/44. Same bug fixed in Settings.uss (2 declarations), Target/TargetCard.uss (2) and Credits/Credits.uss (2, which also imported with 0 rules). Shell.uss was already clean - its author had converted by hand and left the note '/* 0.35em of 13px; USS has no em on letter-spacing */', which is why the login screen was the one screen that looked right. ALSO fixed here: `color: inherit` on `.pl-item.new-hero Label` is not a USS keyword - it parses to a Keyword handle and UITK's own ComputedStyle.ApplyProperties then logs 'Trying to read value of type Color while reading a value of type Keyword' on EVERY style pass; dropped, since `color` is an inherited property in USS anyway. UiShotProbe now prints a UISHEET line per .uss with its real rule count and fails if any imports empty - that guard is the point, the em conversion is just today's instance.

FIX, no new JS coverage claimed. The login CTA rendered as a blank cyan slab with no '▶ შესვლა' on it. A Button IS a TextElement, and UI Toolkit draws a TextElement's own text from ITS generateVisualContent - so `_btnAuth.generateVisualContent += ...` (the .cta-btn clip-path slab, style.css:1457) runs AFTER the glyphs and paints over them. The caption moved to a child Label (`btn-auth-label`); a child is drawn after its parent's content, and colour, font and letter-spacing are inherited USS properties so .cta-btn's own rule still styles it with no duplication. RULE recorded in the file: never add generateVisualContent to a Button or a Label - paint on a plain VisualElement and put the text in a child. Audited the other 14 paint sites in Scripts/UI: every one targets a plain VisualElement, so this was the only instance.

VERIFICATION INFRASTRUCTURE, covers=0. Fixes docs/open_items.json row sweep-contamination: PlayableProbe failed inside the 85-probe VerifyPass4Probe sweep with tick300NoLoggedError (errors=300) while passing standalone with TICK_LOGGED_ERROR_COUNT=0. ROOT CAUSE, read directly: Combat/RangeBootstrap.cs:311 `public static readonly List<Range> All` is never cleared, each Range holds RangeDoorsPaper.Door/.Paper records whose Pivot is a scene Transform, and DiscoverAndAdoptAll() APPENDS. Editor/Probes/RangeFireProbe.cs builds a synthetic GameObject literally named 'warehouse_range' (:112), calls DiscoverAndAdoptAll() (:280) which finds and adopts it, then game.BeginSession() (:302) which adopts it again via GameLoop.cs:404, then DestroyImmediate(holder) (:313). `All` is left holding Ranges whose every Pivot is a destroyed Transform. PlayableProbe then opens Game.unity and ticks 300 frames; GameLoop -> RangeBootstrap.TickAll -> RangeDoorsPaper.Tick hits `p.At = p.Pivot.position` (RangeDoorsPaper.cs:94, a READ of a destroyed Transform) and throws MissingReferenceException - once per tick, because the throw aborts the foreach over All. 300 ticks = 300 errors, exactly. FIX, Editor-side so no production file is touched: [InitializeOnLoad] hooks on EditorSceneManager.sceneClosing/sceneOpened clear RangeBootstrap.All (a public static, so no new API), and PruneDeadRanges() - called by VerifyPass4Probe between every probe - drops Ranges with a destroyed Transform, which covers RangeFireProbe destroying its holder WITHOUT a scene change. PlayableProbe was ADDED to the sweep's Order, deliberately LAST, so every other probe gets its chance to contaminate it first. NOT FIXED HERE, and it is a real game bug, not just a probe one: GameLoop.BeginSession calls DiscoverAndAdoptAll() every session, so the back-to-personages-and-re-enter path (Boot.BackToCharacterSelect -> EnterWorldWithSelectedHero) double-adopts the same ranges and leaves the previous scene's dead ones behind. The production fix is one line - `All.Clear();` as the first statement of DiscoverAndAdoptAll - in Combat/RangeBootstrap.cs, which is another agent's file this pass.

That is Core/ and Combat/, not UI/, so it is reported rather than half-wired.
